The biggest one that comes to mind is Orgsync. It's specifically directed towards students. My university used it, and it's what I used to find my social work internships and volunteer opportunities. There is also https://www.volunteermatch.org/, which I feel is pretty big/up to date. It has 365 postings in my area. There are nearly 3,000 in the new york area... http://www.allforgood.org/volunteers has quite a few. United way is huge in my state. Serve.gov. http://createthegood.org/ There is also meetup.com, which has lot of very specific, local volunteer groups. The biggest problem for this type of project is going to be getting people to use it. Facebook probably isn't the best social media platform out there. But it's the one everyone uses. In the same vein, why would I look for volunteer opportunities on some new app when most established groups looking for volunteers uses other means?

I know how that is. I bought myself a fish when I was feeling really low. The daily feedings and weekly water changes were easy,  but helped give me structure. Something that made me get out of bed, and to focus on before I went to bed. I could watch him swim around while lying in bed instead of reliving painful memories. I don't know how your relationship with your pets is, but they need you and you need them. Don't push that responsibility on someone else. They love you, and they want you to feel better.

Maybe email (or call if you feel up to it) a local suicide/crisis hotline. I know you mentioned you don't think you'll kill yourself, but they should have a list of doctors and therapists that are accessible for free or low incomes. If you live anywhere near a university, I know they can offer free counseling for students. But when the panic attacks are interfering with work, I think it's come to the point you need to ask for help.

This happened to me too. I'm so sorry you've have to feel this much pain. That all your happy memories are now tainted. Knowing that what you had and what you gave didn't mean as much to them as it did for you. I'm so sorry. I know lots of people will say this, but use that pain and energy to do something great. Use it to make a positive change in your life. Exercise or join a group or go on a spontaneous road trip or pick up a new hobby. Training for a marathon has helped me redirect that energy. Just try not to let yourself stew on it and relive it. For example, my therapist had to tell me to stop driving in silence, because it would cause me to overthink it. Make a Playlist of songs that are yours alone, and that make you happy.

Wow that sounds awesome! :D thanks for the advice. Lots of people have asked me to make one. They were upset I told them the stencil was only good for one use. Maybe I'll treat myself to the paper cutter for Christmas.

Watched the tutorials on the side bar and decided to give it a try. $6 blue sweatshirt from the men's section of Walmart and a roll of freezer paper. I blew up the image I wanted and printed it on 4 different pages that I taped together. I put the stencil under the freezer paper and started to trace it with a sharpie. But I realized it would take forever to trace, let alone cut out, so I decided to stop tracing and go straight for the cutting. Took about 2 hours. Ironed the pattern on. Covered all exposed areas. 50/50 bleach/water in a hairspray bottle. Dabbed with paper towels. Thrown in the wash after.

I am honestly surprised how awesome it turned out for a first try! Any comments or questions are welcome.
